title: Fix #97: Infer provider from model name when only model is specified
body:
When users specified only model names (e.g., --fileModel=gemini-2.0-pro), we defaulted to 'gemini' for files but 'openai' for thinking, requiring OpenAI keys unnecessarily. Now we infer providers directly from model names to ensure fix for this specific issue and for similar that may arise. 

Fixes #97

title: Add Xcode command implementation with build, run, and lint functionality
body:
# Add Xcode Command Implementation

This PR adds a new `xcode` command to cursor-tools that enables building, running, and linting iOS apps directly from the command line. The implementation provides robust device state management, error handling, and real-time output streaming.

## Features

### Build Command (`cursor-tools xcode build`)
- Automatic project/workspace detection
- Real-time build output streaming
- Comprehensive error parsing and reporting
- Support for both .xcodeproj and .xcworkspace

### Run Command (`cursor-tools xcode run [device]`)
- Smart device state management
  - Detects already running simulators
  - Handles device state transitions (Shutdown → Booted)
  - Provides clear device state logging
- Configurable simulator device selection
  - `run iphone` - Latest iPhone (15 Pro Max)
  - `run ipad` - Latest iPad (Pro 13-inch)
- Automatic app bundle detection in DerivedData
- Handles app installation and launch

### Lint Command (`cursor-tools xcode lint`)
- Warning analysis and reporting
- SwiftLint integration
- Provides common fix suggestions
- Interactive warning resolution

## Implementation Details

### Core Components
- `XcodeCommand`: Main orchestrator that handles subcommands
- `BuildCommand`: Handles project building and error reporting
- `RunCommand`: Manages simulator lifecycle and app deployment
- `LintCommand`: Analyzes code and suggests improvements
- `utils.ts`: Shared utilities for project detection and error types

### Key Features
- Generator pattern for real-time output streaming
- Robust error handling with descriptive messages
- Smart device state detection and management
- Automatic DerivedData path resolution
- Comprehensive logging for debugging

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Build the project
cursor-tools xcode build

# Run on iPhone simulator
cursor-tools xcode run iphone

# Run on iPad simulator
cursor-tools xcode run ipad

# Analyze and fix warnings
cursor-tools xcode lint
```

## Testing
- Tested with:
  - New iOS projects with .xcodeproj
  - Existing projects with .xcworkspace
  - Different simulator states (fresh/running)
  - Various build scenarios (clean/incremental)
  - Error conditions (missing project, build failures)

## Future Improvements
1. Add archive command for creating .ipa files
2. Add TestFlight submission support
3. Add custom scheme selection
4. Add support for custom simulator configurations
5. Add support for device-specific build settings

## Dependencies
- Requires Xcode and Xcode Command Line Tools
- Optional: SwiftLint for enhanced code analysis

## Breaking Changes
None. This is a new feature that doesn't affect existing functionality.

I've reviewed the PR and noticed that the bundle ID and app name were hardcoded. I've implemented a fix that dynamically determines these values from the project settings. 

The changes include:
1. New getBundleIdentifier method to extract bundle ID from Info.plist or build settings
2. New getAppName method to get app name from Xcode build settings
3. Updated findAppBundle to use dynamic app name instead of hardcoded 'PapersApp.app'
4. Added fallback methods for more reliable app and bundle ID detection

title: feat: consolidate llm service providers to only need 1 api key to use cursor-tools
body:
Release of cursor-tools version 0.5.0 means 3 separate api keys are now needed to make best use of cursor-tools.
These are:
Gemini for thinking & repo compression tasks.
Perplexity for search
Anthropic /  OpenAI for stagehand browser control

I suggest that:
1. A suitably capable llm service provider is chosen for core functionality in cursor-tools.
2. The number of api keys required is consolidated to as few as possible (ideally just 1).

This will make tool adoption for new users a lot easier.
